spatial_claims.claim: C lies between A and B on straight line AB
D is on extension of CA beyond A, with AD = AC, giving collinear order D-A-C-B
CD = 2*AC (since CD = CA + AD = AC + AC)
E lies on segment CD cutting it in extreme and mean ratio, with CE the greater segment; since CE/CD ≈ 0.618 and CE > AC, E lies between A and D, giving order D-E-A-C-B
Application of 13.1: since AC = CD/2, the square on (CE + AC) equals five times the square on AC
CE + AC = AB (positive lengths with equal squares)
AB = AC + CB (from C between A and B), so CE = CB

configuration_map: All points lie on a single line with collinear order D-E-A-C-B. Key relationships: AD = AC, so A is the midpoint of DC. CD = 2*AC. E is on segment CD with CE the greater segment of the EMR cut, so CE ≈ 1.236*AC, placing E between A and D. The proof applies 13.1 to the line CD cut at E, with AC serving as half of CD. The configuration involves only betweenness relations on a single line with no angles, triangles, circles, or complex spatial structures.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The proof operates entirely on a single line with simple betweenness and segment-length relations. The critical geometric step — applying Proposition 13.1 to CD cut at E with AC as half the whole — is correctly configured. The remaining reasoning is algebraic manipulation of squared lengths. No angle decompositions, interior/exterior claims, or complex configurations are present to create contradictions.
